title: DUCK-Net: automated deep learning segmentation of ductular reactions in murine liver injury captures multicellular niche dynamics from H&E morphology

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《DUCK-Net: automated deep learning segmentation of ductular reactions in murine liver injury captures multicellular niche dynamics from H&E morphology》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · path70113-sec-0001-p1】Cholestatic liver diseases such as primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), and other cholangiopathies are associated with the expansion of periportal ductular cells, known histologically as the ductular reaction (DR) [1, 2]. In addition to the proliferation and/or hyperplasia of biliary epithelial cells (BECs) and hepatic progenitor cells (HPCs), DRs are characterised by fibrogenesis and infiltration of stromal and inflammatory cells including macrophages into the periportal regions [3]. DR expansion has been shown to be accompanied by angiogenesis [4] and, in certain contexts, transdifferentiation of hepatocytes [5, 6]. Deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM), in particular laminin, within the DR maintains a local ‘niche’ to determine the cell fate of HPCs and modify the cellular response according to injury aetiology [7]. Further to the well‐established association with biliary injury, DRs can also be observed in the context of severe hepatocyte damage, including alcoholic hepatitis and metabolic dysfunction‐associated liver disease (MASLD), and the extent of DR can act as a histological correlate of disease severity and patient mortality [3, 8, 9].

【Introduction · path70113-sec-0001-p2】Dietary 3,5‐diethoxycarbonyl‐1,4‐dihydro‐collidine (DDC) in mice recapitulates the effects of human cholestatic disease by inducing periportal injury through the induction of interlobular biliary obstruction with protoporphyrin plugs. Toxic accumulation of bile acids activates BECs and initiates periportal inflammation and fibrosis, as well as secondary hepatocyte damage, as evidenced by raised serum transaminases and parenchymal necrosis [10, 11]. BECs upregulate genes that trigger recruitment and differentiation of macrophages, further stimulating BEC proliferation, as well as inducing HPC differentiation into BECs and dampening the proliferation of periportal hepatocytes [12]. The consistent induction of periportal DRs by DDC within weeks of feeding and the resultant recovery following dietary withdrawal have made it a frequently used model of liver injury and regeneration, and its spatiotemporal dynamics have been widely studied [12].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《DUCK-Net: automated deep learning segmentation of ductular reactions in murine liver injury captures multicellular niche dynamics from H&E morphology》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Animal experiments · path70113-sec-0004-p1】C57BL/6 mice were bred in‐house at the University of Edinburgh, UK, and housed in pathogen‐free conditions. At 6–8 weeks old, female mice were fed 0.1% 3,5‐diethoxycarbonyl‐1,4‐dihydro‐collidine for up to 21 days and placed back on standard chow for the recovery model. Four mice were culled at six timepoints. Mice fed normal chow were used as a baseline control group. Sample size was calculated a priori based on published Krt19+ area quantification data from Fickert et al in the DDC model [17]. Assuming group means of 5 (control), 8 (peak injury), and 6 (recovery) arbitrary units with a pooled standard deviation (SD) of 1, the effect size (Cohen's f) was 1.25. Using one‐way ANOVA with α = 0.05% and 80% power, n = 4 mice per group were deemed to be required, providing 91% power to detect significant differences across the injury‐recovery time course. In total, 24 mice were bred specifically for the DDC time course reported in this study. A further 61 archival H&E‐stained sections each from independent mice that had undergone 21 days of DDC dietary injury as control groups in other in‐house studies were included for DUCK‐Net training (one whole‐slide image), validation (50 whole‐slide images), and testing (10 whole‐slide images). For cross‐model generalisation, archival H&E‐stained sections were obtained from mice subjected to two further models of liver injury: a methionine‐choline‐deficient (MCD) diet for 2 weeks (n = 9) and a choline‐deficient diet supplemented with 0.15% ethionine in the drinking water [choline‐deficient, ethionine‐supplemented (CDE) diet] for 6 weeks followed by 2 weeks of recovery on standard chow (n = 6) [18, 19].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《DUCK-Net: automated deep learning segmentation of ductular reactions in murine liver injury captures multicellular niche dynamics from H&E morphology》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · path70113-sec-0010-p1】To evaluate the ability of DUCK‐Net to quantify DRs from H&E morphology, we first assessed model performance against expert pathologist annotations on an independent test set of 10 diverse mouse liver sections selected to represent varying DR severities and tissue morphologies following 21 days of DDC dietary injury. Visual comparison demonstrated apparent close spatial concordance between DUCK‐Net predictions and pathologist‐annotated DR regions on both the initial training slide (Figure 1A,B) and the test set (Figure 1C), including accurate delineation around regions of small and large ducts, anastomosing ductular networks, and interface regions between portal tracts and parenchyma (Figure 1C). Quantitative evaluation across the test set demonstrated robust performance (supplementary material, Table S2), achieving a Dice coefficient of 0.85 ± 0.05 (Jaccard index 0.74), with consistency across diverse tissue appearances and staining variations (Figure 1D). Training curves demonstrated effective learning of the model, with validation loss decreasing rapidly initially before plateauing, indicating successful model convergence without overfitting over 88 epochs of training (Figure 1E). The model achieved robust performance metrics across the test set (Figure 1F; individual sample data is provided in the supplementary material, Table S2): precision 0.84 ± 0.07, recall 0.88 ± 0.08, mean pixel accuracy (MPA) 0.96 ± 0.01, and, notably, specificity was high (0.98 ± 0.01), indicating excellent discrimination against false positive detection.

【Results · path70113-sec-0010-p2】To contextualise the performance of DUCK‐Net for DR detection, we benchmarked its performance against four established CNN‐based segmentation architectures: U‐Net, U‐Net++, DeepLabv3+, and MA‐Net [23, 24, 25, 26]. All five architectures achieved closely comparable performance on the test datasets, with Dice coefficients ranging from 0.851 to 0.857 (DUCK‐Net 0.854 ± 0.053) (supplementary material, Table S3, supplementary material, Figure S1). A Friedman test detected no significant difference in Dice scores across architectures [χ 2 (4) = 7.76, p = 0.101; Kendall's W = 0.194]. The inter‐architecture range (0.006) was substantially smaller than the between‐slide variability (0.053). Similar findings were obtained on the validation dataset, where the best Dice scores ranged from 0.809 (DeepLabv3+) to 0.824 (MA‐Net), with DUCK‐Net at 0.821.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《DUCK-Net: automated deep learning segmentation of ductular reactions in murine liver injury captures multicellular niche dynamics from H&E morphology》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1 · path70113-fig-0001】Figure 1 DUCK‐Net accurately quantifies DR from H&E morphology in mouse liver tissue following DDC dietary injury. (A) Representative mouse whole liver section (H&E) following 21 days of DDC treatment with expert pathologist annotations (ground truth) (blue overlay) and DUCK‐net segmentation (yellow overlay) in training and validation regions of initial training slide. Artefact masking and eosin channel enhancement within training dataset. Scale bars, 5 mm. (B) High‐magnification view of DR region as annotated (yellow) by clinical liver histopathologist, capturing epithelial ductular structures and surrounding reactive stroma. Scale bar, 100 μm. (C) Representative H&E and DUCK‐Net predictions from test set showing segmentation across diverse morphologies including large ducts (top) and small ducts (bottom) and interface regions. Scale bars, 200 μm. (D) Dice coefficients for 10 test samples (mean 0.85 ± 0.05) demonstrating consistent performance across varying DR severities. Dashed line indicates mean value. (E) Training and validation loss curves across 88 epochs. Smooth convergence indicates effective learning without overfitting. (F) DUCK‐Net performance across 10 test samples including precision, recall (sensitivity), specificity, and accuracy.

【Figure 2 · path70113-fig-0002】Figure 2 DUCK‐Net and IHC marker quantification across DDC‐induced liver injury and recovery. (A) Schematic of experimental timeline. Mice were fed 0.1% DDC diet for up to 21 days followed by 14 days of recovery on normal chow (n = 4 per timepoint). Figure created in BioRender. Guest, R. (2026) https://BioRender.com/bxexlm6. (B) Representative images of liver sections stained with H&E or IHC staining of markers of DR across the DDC time course: KRT19, SOX9, EpCAM, α‐SMA, and PSR. Scale bars, 200 μm. (C) Quantification of DUCK‐Net coverage and IHC markers across the time course. DUCK‐Net coverage was expressed as percentage coverage on H&E sections. IHC markers were quantified as percentage positive cells (KRT19, SOX9, EpCAM, α‐SMA) or percentage area (PSR). Markers show a progressive increase during injury (Days 0–21) and decline during recovery (Days 28–35). Data are shown as mean ± SE (n = 4 per timepoint).

【Figure 3 · path70113-fig-0003】Figure 3 DUCK‐Net captures DR niche as characterised by IHC markers across a time course of DDC injury and recovery. (A) Correlation matrix showing Pearson correlation coefficients between DUCK‐Net coverage and individual IHC markers (KRT19, α‐SMA, PSR, SOX9, EpCAM). Colour intensity reflects correlation strength (colour scale, left; r = −1 to 1). Significance levels: *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001. (B) Scatter plot of predicted versus actual DUCK‐Net coverage for individual samples. Each point represents one sample, coloured by timepoint (days). Dashed line indicates perfect agreement (y = x); orange line shows linear regression fit with 95% CI. R 2 = 0.88, RMSE = 0.89. (C) DUCK‐Net coverage (actual, blue) versus IHC predicted values (orange, dashed) across the DDC diet injury and recovery time course. Data shown as mean ± SE (n = 4 per timepoint). Model: R 2 = 0.88, F 5,15 = 22.90, p = 1.58 × 10−6. (D) Standardised regression coefficients showing relative contribution of each IHC marker to DUCK‐Net prediction. Significance levels: ns not significant, *p < 0.05, ***p < 0.001. (E) Scatter plot of SOX9 versus KRT19 expression, demonstrating moderate correlation between epithelial markers (r = 0.33, p = 0.15). Line shows linear regression fit with 95% CI. (F) Model residuals (actual − predicted DUCK‐Net coverage) across the time course. Dashed line indicates zero residual; orange line shows LOESS smoothed trend with 95% CI. Positive residuals at Days 14–21 indicate DUCK‐Net exceeds predicted values at peak injury.

sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《DUCK-Net: automated deep learning segmentation of ductular reactions in murine liver injury captures multicellular niche dynamics from H&E morphology》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Data availability statement · path70113-sec-0015-p1】The DUCK‐Net model and analysis code are publicly available at https://github.com/WhatsMyPurpose/ducknet-dr-segmentation. Raw spatial transcriptomic data from Wu et al were accessed from the CNGB Nucleotide Sequence Archive (https://db.cngb.org/cnsa/ accession CNP0003447) and CIRSTA database (https://db.cngb.org/stomics/cirsta/).

【Model architecture, validation, and testing · path70113-sec-0007-p1】Full details on model architecture and training are provided in the Supplementary materials and methods. Code for the DUCK‐Net model and analysis have been made publicly available at: https://github.com/WhatsMyPurpose/ducknet-dr-segmentation. Model validation was performed at the end of each training epoch using full‐image inference on the validation set. Final model performance was evaluated on the held‐out test set of 10 annotated samples, which were not used during training or hyperparameter selection. Final statistics for annotated pixels and tissue coverage in the training, validation, and test datasets are reported in the supplementary material, Table S1.
